trust_decision.summary: The multipart body parser decides which bytes of a part belong to the inspected value. It holds back a trailing CR/LF in a reserve (possible boundary prefix) and must prepend it to the next chunk when no boundary follows. The form-data branch overwrote the reserve, so embedded line breaks vanished from ARGS/ARGS_POST before rule inspection.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'form-field values' and 'strips line breaks'. The MULTIPART_FORMDATA branch of process_part_data builds each value chunk from the reserve plus the buffer.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory names form-field values (ARGS). FILES_TMP_CONTENT is file-upload content, the on-disk temp file is written correctly with the reserve (multipart.cc:607-624), and the variable only exists when SecUploadKeepFiles or SecTmpSaveUploadedFiles is on, so a solver can call it a separate, opt-in feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The CR/LF just before a boundary is the delimiter, not data. It must stay out of the value: the reserve is dropped when the part ends. A fix that always appends the trailing CRLF, or that stops reserving, adds a stray \r\n to every value and breaks @streq/@eq matches and existing regression tests.

O6_input_shapes: CRLF (2-byte reserve) embedded in a form-data value
bare LF (1-byte reserve) embedded in a form-data value
multiple embedded line breaks in one value (each chunk carries its reserve)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: In the MULTIPART_FILE branch, m_value (later exposed as FILES_TMP_CONTENT) is appended from m_buf only. The reserved CR/LF is written to the temp file but never added to m_value, so embedded line breaks are stripped from the inspected file content, which is the same flaw as in the fixed form-data branch.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory scopes it to form-field values. The file on disk is correct (lines 607-624), and the variable needs opt-in upload config (lines 549-552).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Same file and function, about 40 lines above the fixed line, in the sibling branch

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the parts-joining loop could rebuild m_value from the parts without the reserve carried in m_value_parts (for example, a trim of the trailing CR/LF per part)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer 'normalising' chunk boundaries here is plausible because the code already handles reserve bookkeeping in two places

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the FILES_TMP_CONTENT value could instead be re-read or derived from parts in a way that drops reserved bytes
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The file and form-data paths already diverge on how they build m_value

O9_family: input canonicalisation / parser differential (WAF view of the body differs from the backend's view)

O10_build.toolchain: autotools (build.sh, configure, make), g++, libpcre2, optional yajl/libxml2/lua/geoip
O10_build.project_tests: test/regression runner with JSON cases: test/test-cases/regression/request-body-parser-multipart-crlf.json and test/test-cases/regression/request-body-parser-multipart.json; FILES_TMP_CONTENT appears only in test/test-cases/regression/offset-variable.json
